patients.eight_am_line: Discharged Thu 5 Nov after acute-on-chronic HFrEF. Plan TOC SLA: reach within 2 business days — Friday's voicemail was attempt 1; today is the last day. Two DUR overrides on Friday's fills that nobody told the plan about: lisinopril on top of sacubitril/valsartan (ACEi/ARNI) and KCl on top of a new MRA with no repeat potassium ordered. Call the home line now (attempt 2, inside the window); if no answer, hand Ruth's cell to the evening team for 18:00 (attempt 3). On the call: reinforce the discharge list (lisinopril and KCl are STOPPED), notify Dr Nakamura and Dr Farrow of the auto-refills today, ask the prescriber to order a repeat potassium, and book the cardiology visit by the plan's 7-day target (12 Nov) — the visit's med rec closes HEDIS TRC (30-day measure window); this call alone does not.

patients.name: Priya Lambert
patients.scenario: Three weeks after a delivery complicated by severe pre-eclampsia: a severe-range home BP (164/102) sat in the vendor's weekend inbox; PHQ-9 of 14 is in the OB note but not in the plan's ECDS feed yet; the newborn's claims are billed on her ID

patients.eight_am_line: Delivered 19 Oct with severe pre-eclampsia. Her home cuff read 164/102 on Saturday 19:30 — severe range by systolic — and the vendor's alert went to a programme inbox nobody reads at weekends; the batch file reached us at 06:00. Call now (she consented to texts; use text only if no answer): headache, visual change, RUQ pain or breathlessness → L&D triage today; otherwise a repeat reading on the call and OB notified for same-day evaluation if ≥160 systolic or ≥110 diastolic. PHQ-9 was 14 on 29 Oct — in the OB note, not yet in the ECDS feed, so PND-E follow-up never opened: book the behavioural-health follow-up before 28 Nov. Ignore the three newborn claims on her ID for her risk; task the plan to issue the baby's own ID.

patients.name: Eleanor Vasquez-Hart
patients.scenario: Dual-eligible with moderate Alzheimer's, HFpEF, AF, CKD3b on 11 medications; two sedative-hypnotics from two prescribers four days after a fall (DUR override at the counter); daughter is the effective contact and reportedly holds POA, nothing on file; member file says English, she is Spanish-dominant; home-health start-of-care pended; HRA wrongly flagged non-compliant
patients.feature_stressed: Representative/consent status + language mismatch + duplicate therapy via DUR + pended institutional claim vs care plan + HRA compliance from clinical evidence
patients.eight_am_line: Fell on 26 Oct (ED, home). Since then urgent care added temazepam on top of the PCP's zolpidem — the PBM DUR flagged therapeutic duplication and the pharmacist overrode it; nobody told the plan. Both outreach calls reached Eleanor in English; the PCP note says she is Spanish-dominant now and that Carmen holds healthcare POA (no copy on file). On 28 Oct Eleanor herself asked us to call Carmen — a documented verbal agreement under 164.510(b)(2); because she was confused on that call, Maria also records professional judgement under (b)(3) and asks compliance to confirm — so talking to Carmen about her care is allowed today. Call Eleanor first in Spanish, then Carmen: get the POA copy, tell her the PCP will call about the sleeping tablets (notify Dr Farrow and the plan pharmacist now; do not advise holding anything), chase Lanterne Home Health for the face-to-face note behind the pended start-of-care claim, add the home-health goal to the care plan, and transcribe the HRA Carmen already completed by phone on 3 Sep.
